claim: Two named framings (object+category+rule vs field+relation+context) are a coherent, usable pair of alternative framings for a reasoner.
agent_test: Add a forced second pass that re-describes a problem in the other framing; compare accuracy vs a second sample of the same framing at equal tokens.

claim: Early lab effects (scene description, recognition, change blindness) showed East Asians reporting more background and relations; Japanese made ~65-70% more background statements (Masuda & Nisbett).
agent_test: Not a test of the agent; context only.

claim: Eye-tracking evidence for the attention difference is mixed: Chua et al. found Chinese looked more at background (21 vs 24 analysed); Evans et al. (N=22+22) failed to replicate with the same task.
agent_test: None. Do not cite eye movement as settled.

claim: The individual-level coherence of 'holistic thinking' is very weak: ten cognitive-style measures correlate mean r=0.038 within groups; first factor 10.69% vs 10% chance.
agent_test: Treat analytic/holistic as task-specific framing choices, not a global mode setting; test per task.

claim: Cultural effect sizes on these tasks are moderate (published mean d=0.62) but a multi-country battery (N=379, 4 sites) found mixed results, two reversals (abstract syllogisms more accurate in East Asia than USA).
agent_test: None.

claim: Classic East-West gaps are not unique to East vs West: Arabs, Mapuche, Sangu, Russians and farmers vs herders also differ, and Westerners (WEIRD) are the outlier.
agent_test: None.

claim: Rice-vs-wheat explanation (Talhelm 2014, N=1162 undergraduates): holistic thought higher in rice provinces, but re-analysis shows sensitivity to sample imbalance and Galton's problem (rice share correlates with linguistic distance, Mantel r=0.27, p=0.02).
agent_test: None.

claim: Priming interdependence or independence does not reliably shift analytic/holistic measures in large-sample lab tests (n=84, n=135) and face-scanning (priming did not change cultural differences).
schema_part: O6 (prompt-based switching is not a given)
agent_test: Test whether a framing prompt (not a persona) changes answers in the agent; do not assume it from human priming.

claim: Language of testing can move holistic responses in humans (Korean 10.97 vs English 5.10 ground items, d=-2.15), supporting the idea that instructions/language are a cue.
agent_test: Vary the prompt language/frame and measure change; compare with Sun & Wang null.

claim: LLMs score more holistic than human norms on the Analysis-Holism Scale and Triadic Categorization (GPT-3.5 AHS 5.35, GPT-4 5.01 vs 4.87; triad relational 0.87/0.85), robust across 14 settings.
agent_test: Replicate the AHS and triad at several temperatures on our agent; one paper only supports this.

claim: Other LLM studies using the same paradigm give conflicting verdicts: Atari et al. found GPT triad choices closest to WEIRD (analytic) humans, Hu et al. found the US model MORE relational than a Chinese model. Direction of LLM 'holism' is unstable across prompts and models. Hu et al. numbers re-verified: direction flips by task (image generation US more objects d=1.01; text description Chinese more objects d=2.42; categorization US more relational d=1.38).
agent_test: Run the triad task with 3 prompt wordings; report variance between wordings, not one number.

claim: Prompt language effects on LLM cognitive style are small and unstable: Lu et al. (2 models, 4-12 items) found Chinese prompts more holistic; Sun & Wang (8 models, 30-60 items) found minimal, inconsistent effects; Hu et al. found cultural reversals.
agent_test: Do not rely on a language or persona switch to produce a different framing; check it empirically.

claim: Image-text models: Japanese prompts make captions modestly more background-first (COCO 5K: 19.2% to 23.6-28.6%); image content mattered more (Japanese photos 59-73% holistic).
agent_test: None for text-only agent.

claim: Hu et al. find the Chinese model attributes more to both collective and individual causes (humans trade off), and RLHF persona flattens affective variance, so LLM 'culture' is not a human cultural profile.
agent_test: None.

claim: Broader LLM cultural alignment follows WEIRD/English-Protestant values; cultural prompting narrows the gap (GPT-4o distance 2.42 to 1.57) but not to zero.
agent_test: Measure whether a cultural-prompt wrapper changes answer accuracy; likely only style.

claim: Multi-persona cultural debate improves cultural-neutrality scores (GPT-4o No Bias Rate 57.6% vs 47.6% direct; 80.0 with 5 agents) but personas drift to conformity in debate. Equal-compute work on generic multi-agent debate finds it usually does not beat CoT or Self-Consistency (win rate under 20% in 36 scenarios), so gains need an equal-token control.
agent_test: Equal-token test: 3 framings in one call vs 3 samples of one framing, on a non-cultural reasoning benchmark.

claim: No study found that uses an analytic/holistic framing switch to improve accuracy on reasoning benchmarks; the value for the agent is untested. Nearest analogue: step-back abstraction prompting helps principle-heavy tasks (MMLU Physics +6.8 to +15 points) but not StrategyQA (82.8 to 82.7).
agent_test: Gap: run the equal-token test above.

claim: Debate between multiple LLM agents (including persona debate) usually fails to beat Chain-of-Thought or Self-Consistency at similar token cost; model heterogeneity helps, more agents or rounds do not.
agent_test: Any forced second framing must be compared with a second independent sample of the same framing at equal tokens.

claim: Preregistered tests (11 countries N=993; Czech validation N=392) do not support the analytic/holistic theory as measured: country differences do not follow the East-West labels, and the self-report AHS has an unsatisfactory factor structure.
agent_test: Use task-based probes, not the AHS, if the agent's style is ever scored.

claim: A framing switch helps where the task fits it: abstraction-first (principles) prompting gave large gains on physics, chemistry and TimeQA and none on StrategyQA. No holistic counterpart has been tested for task fit.
agent_test: Per task type, compare analytic-first, holistic-first and plain at equal tokens; report which tasks gain.

claim: The dialectical component (midway, tolerance of contradiction) holds up as its own construct: country-level meta-analysis (k=139, N=23,629, 28 countries) and a revised scale that separates Midway and Contradiction, while Perception of Change loaded negatively on the holism factor. No study links it to reasoning accuracy.
agent_test: Test a contradiction-tolerant pass (hold both claims, seek a midway) separately from a context-attention pass.

claim: Task goals and context can override cultural style: UK and Malaysian drivers showed no change-detection difference while safety relevance had a strong effect; relational mobility is a competing explanation for style differences.
agent_test: Choose framing from task features, not from a persona or culture label.
